title: playing sonar-controlled co-op with myself: two phones, two hands, one cardboard wall
author: FotoRe_store
selftext:
its a game in my sonar collection, you hit a shuttlecock in high arcs with your palm in the air. the phone speaker plays ultrasound and the mic hears the echo from your hand. now two people can play it, each with their own phone and own racket, shared score. you connect on the same wifi or with a 4 digit code over the internet

two things were tricky. first, two sonars next to each other hear each other, so the phones use different tones, one takes the even ones and the other the odd ones, and now the other phone is 25 to 30 db quieter on each mic. second, the network. each phone runs the whole game by itself, your own palm counts right away, and the other palms data comes a bit later, so when it arrives the phone goes back and recalculates those steps. claude told me fighting games do it the same way

in the video i play both sides myself. when the phones are close each sonar starts seeing both hands, so i put a big piece of cardboard between them lol. with two real people they just need to sit a bit apart

im not a programmer, claude wrote all the code, i tested on my iphone and an old mi 9. free in the browser

Play: [https://sonaroids.app](https://sonaroids.app) (game "SonaLob")  
Source: [https://github.com/neokrasav4ik/sonaroids](https://github.com/neokrasav4ik/sonaroids)
